State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Air India vs Sh. Darshan Pal Singh & Anr. on 21 August, 2023
ADDITIONAL BENCH

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 PUNJAB, CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No.918 of 2022
 Date of institution : 28.10.2022
 Reserved on : 09.08.2023
 Date of decision : 21.08.2023

1. Air India Limited through its Principle Officer/authorized officer at
 Rajasansi Airport, Amritsar.
2. Air India Limited, Head Office, New Delhi.
 .....Appellants/Opposite parties No.1&2
 Versus

1. Sh. Darshan Pal Singh S/o Sh. Harbhajan Singh, resident of H.No.C-
 209, East Mohan Nagar, Amritsar.
2. Smt. Harjeet Kaur wife of Sh. Darshan Pal Singh resident of H.No. C-
 209, East Mohan Nagar, Amritsar.
 ....Respondent/complainant

 First Appeal under
Section 41
of the
 Consumer Protection Act, 2019
 against the order dated 20.09.2022 of
 the District Consumer Disputes
 Redressal Commission, Amritsar
 Quorum:-
 Mr. H.P.S. Mahal, Presiding Judicial Member
Mrs. Kiran Sibal, Member

 Present:-
For the appellants : Sh. D.P. Azad, Advocate
 For the respondents : Sh. Dharampal Singh, in person

 KIRAN SIBAL, MEMBER

 The instant appeal has been filed by the
appellants/Opposite parties No.1 & 2 against the order dated

 20.09.2022 passed by District Consumer Disputes Redressal

 Commission, Amritsar (in short, "the District Commission"), whereby
FA No. 918 of 2022 2
the complaint filed by complainant against opposite parties (in short

'OP'), under the
Consumer Protection Act
, was allowed and following

relief has been granted:-
"In view of the above discussion, we allow the
 complaint and the opposite parties No.1 & 2 are
 directed to make payment of $1410/- or the amount
 equivalent in Indian currency alongwith interest@6%
 p.a. from the date of filing of the complaint till its
 realization. As the complainants have suffered a lot
 due to departure of the flight on 6.10.2018 as they had
 to wait for two days for the journey from New Delhi to
 Auckland International Airport by spending another
 amount i.e. $1450/-, as such the opposite parties No.1
 & 2 are also liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,000/-
 as well as litigation expenses of Rs.10,000/- to the
 complainants. As no case is made out against
 opposite party No.3 as they fulfilled their duty by
 making arrangement of the tickets for the
 complainants, as such complaint against opposite
 party No.3 sands dismissed."
2. It would be apposite to mention that hereinafter the parties

will be referred, as have been arrayed before the District Commission.
3. Brief facts for the disposal of the appeal are that the

complainants booked two airways tickets from OP No.3 bearing Nos.

0982987149426 and 0982987149425 to travel from Amritsar Airport

to Indira Gandhi, Airport, New Delhi and paid a sum of Rs.10,602/- for

the said tickets. They were to travel in the flight of Air India bearing

No.AI-454 on 06.12.2018 at 6.50 AM. After reaching at New Delhi

Airport, the complainants were to further travel from New Delhi to

Auckland International Airport through China Southern Airlines in their

flight No.CZ3028 vide ticket Nos.7844444166618 & 7844444166631

on the same day at 12:35 PM. On 06.12.2018 the complainants

entered in the Airport, Amritsar within stipulated time to take their flight
FA No. 918 of 2022 3
No.AI-454 but the said flight was delayed by five hours and it reached

at New Delhi Airport at 1:00 PM. When the complainants approached

the concerned terminal of Indira Gandhi Airport, New Delhi, to take

their flight from New Delhi to Auckland, the officers of Airlines told that

they were late and their flight had already departure at 6:30 PM and

their tickets had been cancelled. There was no fault of the

complainants but the flight was missed only due to delayed flight of Air

India Limited. The complainants were left with no other option except

to purchase new tickets to travel to the said destination on 08.12.2018

and had to pay $1450. The complainants approached many times to

refund the said amount but to no avail. Alleging deficiency in service

on the part of OPs, filed a consumer complaint and sought directions

against the OPs to pay cost of cancelled tickets to the tune of $1410

along with interest @ 18% p.a. and further to pay Rs.1,00,000/- as

compensation.
4. In reply to the complaint, OPs No.1 & 2 stated that the

flight in question had to reach at Amritsar from Delhi and had flown in

time but due to bad weather condition, it had to go back to Delhi

Airport. Accordingly, on receiving such information by the authorities,

the passengers including the complainants were duly informed

regarding the reason "Aircraft from previous sector delayed due to bad

weather condition", as such the delay occurred due to bad weather

condition and there was no fault of the Airlines/Airport authorities. As

per DGCA rules, it is provided in clause 1.4 "The operating Airlines

would not have the obligation to pay compensation in cases where the
FA No. 918 of 2022 4
cancellations and delays have been caused by an event of force

majeure i.e. extra-ordinary circumstances beyond the control of the

Airlines". In the log book dated 06.12.2018 it was specifically

mentioned that due to bad weather condition "Below Minima", the

flight in question had gone back to Delhi and could not reach Amritsar

in time and the concerned passengers of that flight were duly informed

by the Airport authorities. The complainants and other passengers

were provided proper refreshment free of cost. Since, the

complainants were informed well in time, they were at liberty to get

their tickets cancelled and to get refund. There was no deficiency in

service on the part of OPs No.1 & 2. After denying the other averments

made in the complaint, OPs No.1 & 2 prayed for dismissal of the

complaint.
5. In reply to the complaint, OP No.3 stated that the

complainants were not the "Consumers" as provided under the Act, as

they filed a joint complaint and no prior permission has been taken

from the District Commission to file the same jointly. There was no

deficiency in service on the part of OP No.3. After denying the other

averments made in the complaint, OP No.3 prayed for dismissal of the

complaint, qua it.
6. The parties led their evidence in support of their respective

contentions and the District Commission after going through the record

and hearing learned counsel for the parties, allowed the complaint of

the complainants against OPs No. 1 & 2, vide impugned order as
FA No. 918 of 2022 5
above. Aggrieved with the same, the present appeal has been filed by

the appellants/OPs No.1 & 2 for setting aside the same.
7. We have heard the Ld.counsel for the parties and have

carefully gone through the written submissions filed by them and the

record of the case.
8. The learned counsel for the appellants/OPs No. 1 & 2

vehemently contended that the District Commission has failed to

consider the fact that the appellants had flown the flight in question

from Delhi to Amritsar in time but due to bad weather conditions, it had

gone back to Delhi and the passengers were duly informed about the

delay in flight. The learned counsel further contended that as per

DGCA rules, under Clause 1.4, the operating Airlines could not have

obligation to pay compensation in cases where the cancellations and

delays have been caused by an event of force majeure i.e. extra-

ordinary circumstances beyond the control of the Airlines. Accordingly,

there was no fault of the Airlines/Airport authorities in the present case

as delay was caused due to bad weather which was beyond the

control of the OPs. Alleging no deficiency in service on their part, the

learned counsel for OPs No.1 & 2 prayed for acceptance of the

present appeal by setting aside the impugned order.
9. On the other hand, the respondents in their written

arguments, stated that the order passed by the District Commission is

a well reasoned and speaking order. The appellants failed to prove on

record that there was any alleged bad weather condition due to which
FA No. 918 of 2022 6
the flight had to go back to Delhi. There is no iota of evidence to show

that the appellants had disclosed about the delay to the

respondents/complainants as alleged. No arrangements were made by

the appellants to adjust the passengers to travel in the alternative

flights, which departure from Raja Sansi Airport at 9:07 AM, 9:23 AM

and 10:12 AM on 06.12.2018. Alleging deficiency in service on the part

of the appellants, the respondents prayed for dismissal of the present

appeal.
10. We have given thoughtful consideration to the contentions

raised by the parties.
11. Admitted facts of the case are that the

respondents/complainants booked two tickets bearing

No.0982987149426 and 0982987149425 for travelling from Amritsar to

Indira Gandhi Airport, New Delhi in flight No.AI-454 on 06.12.2018 and

paid consideration to the tune of Rs.10,602/-(Ex. C-1). The case of the

complainants is that they had reached Amritsar Airport on 06.12.2018

in time but the flight was delayed due to which they reached 'New

Delhi Airport' at 1:00 PM, thereby missing the further flight from New

Delhi to Auckland International Airport. The respondents/complainants

alleged that due to fault of the appellants/OPs No.1&2, they had to

purchase new tickets for Auckland International Airport and had to

spend $1450. On the other hand, the appellants/OPs No.1 & 2

pleaded that the delay in flight was caused due to bad weather, which

was beyond their control and as per DGCA rules under clause 1.4, the

operating airlines would not have the obligation to pay compensation
FA No. 918 of 2022 7
in cases where the cancellations and delays have been caused by an

event of force majeure. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of

the appellants/OPs, the respondents/complainants filed consumer

complaint before the District Commission, which was allowed by it

against the appellants/OPs No.1 & 2, vide impugned order. Aggrieved

with the same the appellants/OP No.1 & 2 filed the present appeal for

setting aside the same.
12. The foremost contention raised by the appellants/OP No.1

& 2 is that the District Commission has failed to consider and

appreciate the fact that the appellants/OPs No. 1 & 2 have duly proved

on record by leading cogent evidence that delay in flight was caused

due to bad weather, which was beyond their control and as per DGCA

rules under clause 1.4, they were not liable to pay any compensation.

To determine this point, we have carefully perused the pleadings and

evidence on record. A perusal of E-Ticket, Ex. C-1, shows that the

complainants booked two tickets for travelling from Amritsar to New

Delhi in flight No.AI-454 on 06.12.2018, which was scheduled to

depart from Amritsar at 6:50 AM and arrive at New Delhi at 7:65 AM. It

is not in dispute that the said flight was delayed and reached late at

New Delhi airport due to which the respondents/complainants missed

the further flight to Auckland. The stand of the appellants/OPs No.1 &

2 is that the said delay was caused due to bad weather conditions and

respondents/complainants were duly informed by the authorities of

Airline at Amritsar in this regard. To support their version, appellants

relied upon Log Book, Ex. OP1-2/5. A perusal of said Log book, Ex.
FA No. 918 of 2022 8
OP1-2/5 shows that the appellants have duly mentioned in the Log

Book that flight No.AI-454 had gone back to Delhi, due to bad weather

in Amritsar "Below Minima". It is also mentioned in the said Log Book

that all the passengers have been duly informed about the delay.

From the perusal of certificate dated 06.12.2018, Ex. C-2, placed on

record by the respondents/complainants, it is proved on record that

they were informed about the fact that Air India Flight AI-454 was

delayed due to bad weather. The appellants/OPs No.1 & 2 further

relied upon guidelines issued by the DGCA,(Ex. OP1-2/3) regarding

facilities to be provided to passengers by airlines due to denied

boarding, cancellation of flights and delays in flights. The relevant

clauses of the said guidelines are reproduced as under:-
" Clause 1.4: The operating airline would not
 have the obligation to pay compensation in cases
 where the cancellations and delay have been caused
 by an event(s) of force majeure i.e. extraordinary
 circumstances(s) beyond the control of the airlines,
 the impact of which lead to the cancellation/delay of
 flight(s) and which could not have been avoided even
 if all reasonable measures had been taken by the
 airline. Such extraordinary circumstances may in
 particular, occur due to political instability, natural
 disaster, civil war, insurrection or riot, flood,
 explosion, government regulation or order affecting
 the aircraft, strikes and labour disputes causing
 cessation, slowdown or interruption of work or any
 other factors that are beyond the control of the
 airline.
Clause 1.5: Additionally, airlines would also not
 be liable to pay any compensation in respect of
 cancellations and delays clearly attributable to Air
 Traffic Control (ATC), meteorological conditions,
 security risks, or any other causes that are beyond
 the control of the airline but which affect their ability
 to operate flights on schedule. Extraordinary
 circumstances should be deemed to exist where the
FA No. 918 of 2022 9
impact of an air traffic management decision in
 relation to a particular aircraft or several aircraft on a
 particular day, gives rise to a long delay or delays, an
 overnight delay, or the cancellation of one or more
 flights by that aircraft, and which could not be
 avoided even though the airline concerned had taken
 all reasonable measures to avoid or overcome of the
 impact of the relevant factor and, therefore, the
 delays or cancellations."
According to above said clauses of DGCA guidelines, Ex. OP1-2/3, the

operating airline would not have the obligation to pay compensation in

cases where the delays have been caused by an event(s) of force

majeure i.e. extraordinary circumstance(s) beyond the control of the

airline. The appellants proved on record, as discussed above, that the

delay in flight caused due to bad weather and complainants were duly

informed regarding the said delay. Moreover, the appellants were also

provided proper refreshment, free of costs during the waiting period on

account of delay of flight. The said fact has not been denied by the

respondents/complainants. The complainants were at liberty to get

their tickets cancelled and to get refund of the amount of tickets and

could make alternate arrangements for their travel to New Delhi. As

such, we are of the considered view that the flight was delayed due to

bad weather which is beyond the control of appellants/OPs and there

is no fault or deficiency in service on the part of the appellants/OPs.

The District Commission has overlooked the above said clauses of

DGCA rules/guidelines and failed to consider and appreciate the facts

that delay in flight was caused due to bad weather, which is beyond

the control of the appellants/OPs. The respondents/complainants have

pleaded, in the written arguments, that no arrangements were made
FA No. 918 of 2022 10
by the appellants to adjust the passengers to travel in the alternative

flights, which depart from Raja Sansi Airport on 06.12.2018 at 9:07

AM, 9:23 AM and 10:12 AM. It is pertinent to mention that here that

this plea has not been taken by the respondents/complainants in the

original complaint before the District Commission and appears to be

an afterthought. Be that as it may, the respondents/complainants have

also not been able to establish, by leading any cogent evidence, that

there was any availability of seats in the said flights. Hence, we find

force in the contention raised by the appellants/OPs No.1& 2 and are

of the opinion that there is no deficiency in service on the part of the

appellants/OPs No.1 & 2 with regard to alleged delay in flight. The

District Commission has wrongly held the appellants/OPs No.1 & 2

deficient in service. As such, the impugned order of the District

Commission is liable to be set aside.
13. Sequel to our above discussion, we allow the appeal of the

appellants/OPs No.1 & 2 and the impugned order of the District

Commission is hereby set aside. The complaint filed by the

respondents/complainants is also dismissed.
14. The appellants had deposited an amount of Rs.25,000/- at

the time of filing the appeal with this Commission. This amount

alongwith interest, which accrued thereon, if any, be remitted by the

Registry to the appellants/OP No.1& 2 by way of demand draft/crossed

cheque, after the expiry of 45 days from the date of receipt of certified

copy of this order, in accordance with law.
FA No. 918 of 2022 11
15. The appeal could not be decided within the stipulated

 period due to heavy pendency of Court cases.
(H.P.S. MAHAL)
 PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER

 (KIRAN SIBAL)
 MEMBER
August 21, 2023.
(Dv)
